List of oldest extant buildings :: Criteria :: chunk_0001
A [building](/wiki/Building "Building") is defined as any human-made structure used or interface for supporting or sheltering any use or continuous [occupancy](/wiki/Occupancy "Occupancy"). In order to qualify for this list, a structure must:

* be a recognisable building;
* incorporate features of building work from the claimed date to at least 1.5 metres (4.9 ft) in height;
* be largely complete or include building work to this height for most of its perimeter.
* contain an enclosed area with at least one entry point.

This deliberately excludes ruins of limited height and statues. The list also excludes:

* [dolmens](/wiki/Dolmen "Dolmen"), a type of single-chamber megalithic tomb, usually consisting of three or more upright stones supporting a large flat horizontal capstone. Dolmens were typically covered with earth or smaller stones to form a [tumulus](/wiki/Tumulus "Tumulus") (which are included in the list). In many instances, that covering has weathered away, leaving only the stone "skeleton" of the burial mound intact. [Neolithic](/wiki/Neolithic "Neolithic") dolmens are extremely numerous, with over 1,000 reported from [Mecklenburg-Vorpommern](/wiki/Megaliths_in_Mecklenburg-Vorpommern "Megaliths in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern") in Germany alone.[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* [cairns](/wiki/Cairn "Cairn"), which are simply large piles of loose stones (as opposed to [chambered cairns](/wiki/Chambered_cairn "Chambered cairn"))
* [standing stone rings](/wiki/Standing_stones "Standing stones"), such as [Stonehenge](/wiki/Stonehenge "Stonehenge"), also do not count because they are not enclosed and do not have roofs.

Dates for many of the oldest structures have been arrived at by [radiocarbon dating](/wiki/Radiocarbon_dating "Radiocarbon dating") and should be considered approximate.

Francis II, Holy Roman Emperor :: Emperor :: Napoleonic Wars :: chunk_0004
During the [War of the Third Coalition](/wiki/War_of_the_Third_Coalition "War of the Third Coalition"), the Austrian forces met a crushing defeat at [Austerlitz](/wiki/Battle_of_Austerlitz "Battle of Austerlitz"), and Francis had to agree to the [Treaty of Pressburg](/wiki/Treaty_of_Pressburg_(1805) "Treaty of Pressburg (1805)"), which greatly weakened Austria and brought about the final collapse of the [Holy Roman Empire](/wiki/Holy_Roman_Empire "Holy Roman Empire"). In July 1806, under massive pressure from France, Bavaria and fifteen other German states ratified the statutes founding the [Confederation of the Rhine](/wiki/Confederation_of_the_Rhine "Confederation of the Rhine"), with Napoleon designated Protector, and they announced to the [Imperial Diet](/wiki/Imperial_Diet_(Holy_Roman_Empire) "Imperial Diet (Holy Roman Empire)") their intention to leave the Empire with immediate effect. Then, on 22 July, Napoleon issued an ultimatum to Francis demanding that he abdicate as Holy Roman Emperor by 10 August.[[10]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWhaley2012643-11)[[11]](#cite_note-12)

Five days later, Francis bowed to the inevitable and, without mentioning the ultimatum, affirmed that since the Peace of Pressburg he had tried his best to fulfil his duties as emperor but that circumstances had convinced him that he could no longer rule according to his oath of office, the formation of the Confederation of the Rhine making that impossible. He added that "we hereby decree that we regard the bond which until now tied us to the states of the Empire as dissolved"[[12]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWhaley2012643–644-13) in effect dissolving the empire. At the same time he declared the complete and formal withdrawal of his hereditary lands from imperial jurisdiction.[[13]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGagliardo1980281-14) After that date, he continued to reign as Francis I, Emperor of Austria.
